claim.quote: no significant TeV gamma-ray signals have been detected from compact regions around PSR B1706-44 or within the northeast rim of SN 1006

date.note: arXiv v1 submission date; journal reference as printed on the arXiv page: Astrophys.J.702:631-648,2009.

name: CANGAROO reanalysis of its 3.8 m telescope data: no significant signal from PSR B1706-44 or SN 1006
notes: The abstract describes the reanalysis of observations "between 1993 and 1998"; the original detections of PSR B1706-44 (Kifune et al., 1995) and SN 1006 are not recorded as results because the collaboration's own reanalysis does not support them.
The original paper for these detections was not fetched, so no original result record is written.

significance.quote: a TeV gamma-ray signal from the Vela pulsar region at the 4.5 sigma level using 1993, 1994, and 1995 data
significance.value: 4.5 sigma (Vela pulsar region, 1993-1995 data); no significant signal for PSR B1706-44 or the northeast rim of SN 1006

summary.plain: The CANGAROO team reanalysed its 3.8 metre telescope data after H.E.S.S. results and found no significant TeV signal from the pulsar PSR B1706-44 or the supernova remnant SN 1006, although a 4.5 sigma excess near the Vela pulsar remained.
summary.technical: Data taken between 1993 and 1998, reanalysed with selection criteria set exclusively from gamma-ray simulations and OFF-source data: no significant signal from compact regions around PSR B1706-44 or in the northeast rim of SN 1006; a 4.5 sigma signal from the Vela pulsar region (HESS J0835-455) from 1993-1995 data.

title: Reanalysis of Data Taken by the CANGAROO 3.8 Meter Imaging Atmospheric Cherenkov Telescope: PSR B1706-44, SN 1006, and Vela
why_it_matters: The collaboration discusses why its original analyses gave the source detections; the abstract states the reanalysis was made in response to the H.E.S.S. results. It revises the collaboration's earlier detections of these sources.
